summary: The sample implements the requested FastAPI cohort-backend, runs the aggregation with $bucket and produces materialised snapshots that the API serves. The run verified seeding, index creation and a successful one-shot snapshot generation against the provided cluster. Main findings: (1) the pipeline does use $bucket successfully in this environment but public docs warn $bucket is unsupported on some Mongo-API server versions — the product docs should be made more prominent to prevent fragile samples; (2) the implementation materialises snapshots but inserts new snapshot documents rather than replacing/upserting previous snapshots; (3) the pipeline computes breakdowns by channel/product but does not use a $facet stage as the prompt suggested; (4) some operational best-practices (explain()/diagnostics, retry/backoff for snapshot writes, RU/throughput guidance and basic instrumentation) are missing. None of the missing items make the sample unusable for demo, but several are important for production-readiness and for agents generating similar samples.

requirement_results.requirement: A Python FastAPI service exposes HTTP endpoints that return cohort analysis results.
requirement_results.evidence: app/app/main.py: lines 24-36 define GET /cohorts and GET /cohorts/{snapshot_month}; lines 39-43 define POST /admin/refresh.

requirement_results.requirement: The cohort computation is an aggregation pipeline that Azure DocumentDB executes, sent through a MongoDB driver (e.g. PyMongo).
requirement_results.evidence: app/app/cohort.py: pipeline defined and executed with customers.aggregate(...); app/scripts/generate_snapshot.py runs generate_cohort_snapshot (app/app/cohort.py: lines 64-146, 145-176).

requirement_results.requirement: The pipeline uses a `$bucket` stage to group customers by acquisition month.
requirement_results.evidence: app/app/cohort.py: $bucket stage present (lines 98-113) with groupBy: "$acquired_at" and boundaries constructed earlier.

requirement_results.requirement: The pipeline computes retention rates at 30, 60 and 90 days for each cohort.
requirement_results.evidence: app/app/cohort.py: retained30/retained60/retained90 computed in $addFields (lines 76-97) and summed in $bucket output (lines 105-108).

requirement_results.requirement: The pipeline uses a `$facet` stage to break the cohorts down by channel and by product.
requirement_results.evidence: app/app/cohort.py: channel and product breakdowns are produced by $push/$arrayToObject mapping after the $bucket stage (lines 109-140, 116-141), but there is no `$facet` stage in the pipeline.
requirement_results.smallest_fix: Replace or augment the post-bucket transformation with an explicit $facet stage that computes channel and product facets (small change in the pipeline definition: add a $facet with two sub-pipelines that $unwind/$group or $sortByCount on channels and products).

requirement_results.requirement: Cohort snapshots are cached as materialised documents stored in Azure DocumentDB (e.g. a snapshots collection), produced by running the pipeline.
requirement_results.evidence: app/app/cohort.py: snapshot document constructed and snapshots.insert_one(snapshot) (lines 168-175). scripts/generate_snapshot.py (lines 8-11) runs the function and prints the result.

requirement_results.requirement: A weekly refresh re-runs the pipeline and replaces the materialised snapshot documents.
requirement_results.evidence: app/app/main.py: BackgroundScheduler schedules weekly_job that calls generate_cohort_snapshot(db) (lines 9-18).
requirement_results.smallest_fix: Change snapshot persistence to upsert/replace (e.g., use update_one(filter={'snapshot_month': ...}, {'$set': snapshot}, upsert=True) instead of insert_one) so a weekly run replaces the previous snapshot rather than inserting a fresh document.

requirement_results.requirement: The cohort endpoints serve their results from the cached snapshot documents.
requirement_results.evidence: app/app/main.py -> api_list_snapshots and api_get_snapshot call list_snapshots/get_snapshot which read from cohort_snapshots (lines 24-36).

requirement_results.requirement: The connection string and model credentials come from environment variables; none appear in the repository.
requirement_results.evidence: app/app/db.py: reads DOCUMENTDB_URI and DB_NAME from environment (lines 5-11). app/.env.example contains placeholders (app/.env.example lines 1-3).

requirement_results.requirement: A `.env.example` lists every setting with placeholder values.
requirement_results.evidence: app/.env.example lists DOCUMENTDB_URI and DB_NAME (app/.env.example lines 1-3).

requirement_results.requirement: The vector index dimensions match the embedding model's output.
requirement_results.evidence: No vector index or embedding model is used by this sample; vectors are out of scope.

requirement_results.requirement: The vector index parameters are chosen for the sample's data size, and the README says how to change them for a larger one.
requirement_results.evidence: No vector search or vector index in the repository.

requirement_results.requirement: One database client is created and reused across requests.
requirement_results.evidence: app/app/db.py: uses a module-level _client and get_client(), returning a singleton MongoClient (lines 13-28).

requirement_results.requirement: A seed script loads sample data and creates the index, and can be run twice without duplicating data.
requirement_results.evidence: app/scripts/seed.py: drops and re-inserts collections (lines 35-38) and creates indexes (lines 77-85). The script is idempotent for demo use (deletes previous sample data then inserts fresh data).

requirement_results.requirement: /search returns a clear error for an empty query and when the embedding call fails.
requirement_results.evidence: This sample exposes cohort endpoints only; no /search endpoint exists.
requirement_results.smallest_fix: If search is later added, add explicit input validation and error handling that returns HTTP 400 for empty queries and 502/503 for embedding failures.

requirement_results.requirement: Search results include the similarity score.
requirement_results.evidence: No search endpoint or vector retrieval implemented in this sample.

requirement_results.requirement: Dependencies are pinned in `requirements.txt`.
requirement_results.evidence: app/requirements.txt pins exact versions (fastapi==0.95.2, uvicorn==0.23.2, pymongo==4.5.0, etc.) (app/requirements.txt lines 1-7).

requirement_results.requirement: Unit tests run without a live cluster.
requirement_results.evidence: app/tests/test_cohort.py uses mongomock and inserts a small in-memory DB for tests; tests do not require a live cluster (app/tests/test_cohort.py shows mongomock usage).

requirement_results.requirement: Infrastructure for the cluster is provided as code, using the Azure DocumentDB resource type.
requirement_results.evidence: No IaC files (Bicep/Terraform/ARM) for Microsoft.DocumentDB/mongoClusters are present in the repository (no templates in repo root).
requirement_results.smallest_fix: Add a small Bicep or Terraform example that creates a Microsoft.DocumentDB/mongoClusters resource (or an ARM template snippet) and documents default low-cost parameters.

requirement_results.requirement: The README covers what the sample shows, prerequisites, setup, run, and clean-up.
requirement_results.evidence: app/README.md includes 'What this sample shows', prerequisites, quick start, API endpoints and cleaning up instructions (README.md lines 1-31, 37-43).

requirement_results.requirement: The sample uses the name "Azure DocumentDB" throughout, and no former or neighbouring product name.
requirement_results.evidence: app/README.md, .env.example and other files refer to 'Azure DocumentDB' (README.md lines 1 and 14; .env.example comments).

checks.practice: Create and reuse a single MongoClient process-wide (singleton) and avoid creating a new client per request; configure pool parameters only after understanding your workload.
checks.evidence: app/app/db.py: uses module-level _client and get_client() to return a singleton MongoClient (lines 13-28).

checks.practice: Tune connection-pool settings to your deployment scenario and set fail-fast timeouts.
checks.evidence: app/app/db.py: sets serverSelectionTimeoutMS and (in a prior write) retryWrites=True; conservative defaults used when constructing MongoClient (lines 19-25 in some app/db.py copies).

checks.practice: Pin the driver version and use a version the service supports.
checks.evidence: app/requirements.txt pins pymongo==4.5.0 (app/requirements.txt line 3). Microsoft docs state DocumentDB supports modern MongoDB wire protocol versions so recent PyMongo 4.x is appropriate.
checks.source: Quickstart: Use Azure DocumentDB with MongoDB driver for Python
checks.searched: search: 'Azure DocumentDB pymongo supported versions quickstart'

sources.title: Quickstart: Use Azure DocumentDB with MongoDB driver for Python

checks.practice: Read the DocumentDB connection string from an environment variable (DOCUMENTDB_URI), never hard-code credentials and keep only a .env.example
checks.evidence: app/app/db.py: DOCUMENTDB_URI read from env (lines 7-11). app/.env.example contains placeholder (app/.env.example lines 1-3). No secrets are checked in.

checks.practice: Keep DB credentials in a secret store and prefer Microsoft Entra (managed identity) + RBAC instead of long-lived DB passwords
checks.evidence: The app reads DOCUMENTDB_URI and uses it for SCRAM auth (app/app/db.py lines 7-11). No OIDC/Microsoft Entra ID flow is implemented.
checks.fix: Document why SCRAM is used in README and add guidance / optional example for MONGODB-OIDC/DefaultAzureCredential (or provide a separate sample that enables Microsoft Entra ID authentication).

checks.practice: Always require TLS for client connections and never disable certificate validation in production.
checks.evidence: app/.env.example suggests mongodb+srv connection string including tls=true and README warns not to commit secrets (app/.env.example & README.md).

checks.practice: Enable driver retryable reads/writes where supported and implement application-level retries with exponential backoff for transient errors.
checks.evidence: The MongoClient is constructed with retryWrites=True in some app/db.py variants in the repo (events show that), but snapshot writes (snapshots.insert_one) are not wrapped with explicit application-level retries or backoff (app/app/cohort.py lines 174-175).
checks.fix: Wrap snapshot persistence in a retry loop with exponential backoff (or use a helper that retries transient errors), and consider capturing and retrying RequestRateTooLarge/429 responses.

checks.practice: Create indexes that support your cohort aggregation and query patterns — index acquisition timestamp and customer identifier and add compound ESR indexes for common filters/sorts.
checks.evidence: app/scripts/seed.py creates indexes on customers.customer_id (unique), customers.acquired_at, customers.channel, customers.primary_product_id and events.customer_id, events.event_date, events.product_id (seed.py lines 77-85).

checks.practice: Prefer aggregation pipelines (server-side aggregation) and verify pipeline performance with explain().
checks.evidence: The app uses aggregation pipelines (good) but the sample does not call explain("executionStats") or capture executionStats to validate index usage and RU-cost (app/app/cohort.py runs customers.aggregate(...) but no explain call).
checks.fix: Add an explain("executionStats") step in scripts/refresh_snapshots.py or a helper that records the aggregation's executionStats to logs or a diagnostics collection so readers can confirm index usage and RU consumption.

checks.practice: Project only required fields early in aggregation pipelines to reduce RU usage.
checks.evidence: The pipeline does a $lookup that pulls full events arrays then filters in-memory; it does not project minimal fields in the $lookup pipeline (app/app/cohort.py lines 66-74 and $lookup).
checks.fix: Use $lookup with a pipeline that $project only the event_date and product/channel fields required, or project fields before expensive stages to limit returned data.

checks.practice: Materialize heavy cohort snapshots as compact summary documents and refresh them on a schedule; perform snapshot writes with batched operations to reduce RU and roundtrips.
checks.evidence: App materializes a compact snapshot document and writes it to cohort_snapshots (app/app/cohort.py lines 168-175). The weekly scheduler is configured (app/app/main.py lines 9-18).
checks.fix: If writing many snapshot documents at once, switch to bulk operations; current single-document snapshots are fine for a demo.

checks.practice: Embed frequently-read attributes (channel, product) in event documents to avoid expensive $lookup joins.
checks.evidence: Seeded documents include channel and primary_product_id fields in customer and product/product_id and channel in events (app/scripts/seed.py lines 44-52 and event docs lines 66-72).

checks.practice: Avoid relying on aggregation stages that may be unsupported by some API-server versions (e.g., $bucket/$bucketAuto) — check compatibility pages.
checks.evidence: The app uses $bucket (app/app/cohort.py lines 98-113) and the one-shot snapshot generation completed successfully in this run (builder_report: 'Generated snapshot: ...'). However Azure docs explicitly warn some aggregation stages may be unsupported on some API-server versions.
checks.source: Azure Cosmos DB feature support (MongoDB) / aggregation pipeline pages
checks.fix: Add a compatibility note to README and add a runtime compatibility test (or an explain/feature-check step) that fails with a clear message if the server does not support $bucket.

sources.title: Azure Cosmos DB feature support (MongoDB) / aggregation pipeline pages

checks.practice: Instrument the service with application-level metrics (snapshot duration, RU consumed per snapshot) and alert on RU throttling.
checks.evidence: No instrumentation or logging of snapshot duration or RU consumption is implemented; generate_cohort_snapshot simply runs the pipeline and inserts snapshot (app/app/cohort.py lines 145-175).
checks.fix: Log snapshot start/end times and capture explain() RU metrics or return executionStats; add a basic metric emit (duration, doc counts, and failure counts) to the snapshot script.

checks.practice: For aggregation facets (channel/product breakdown), design compound indexes matching equality and group keys (ESR rule).
checks.evidence: The app creates single-field indexes that are useful for lookups, but does not create compound ESR indexes specifically tuned for the current facet computation (seed.py lines 77-85). The sample's small dataset is served by single-field indexes; for large data, add compound indexes.
checks.fix: If dataset grows, create compound indexes such as {channel:1, acquired_at:1} or {product_id:1, event_date:1} following ESR guidance.

checks.practice: Prefer incremental/change-feed-driven snapshot updates rather than full recomputes for large datasets.
checks.evidence: The app runs a full recompute weekly (BackgroundScheduler or on-demand), it does not implement incremental or change-feed updates (app/app/main.py lines 9-18 and app/scripts/generate_snapshot.py).
checks.source: Improve efficiency of reads by using a cache / materialize via Stream Analytics and change feed
checks.fix: Document and optionally provide an alternate script that uses the cluster's change feed or change streams to incrementally update snapshots, or show how to run per-cohort partial recomputes.

sources.title: Improve efficiency of reads by using a cache / materialize via Stream Analytics and change feed

checks.practice: Check the Azure Cosmos DB feature-support pages for the server-version you run; aggregation-stage support varies by server version.
checks.evidence: The sample did not add a README note or runtime compatibility check to ensure the server version supports all aggregation stages used (no explain() or server-version check documented).
checks.source: Azure Cosmos DB feature support pages
checks.searched: search: 'Azure DocumentDB aggregation stage $bucket feature support'
checks.fix: Add a short 'compatibility check' step in README (and an optional script) that queries the server for its MongoDB wire version or runs a small feature-check pipeline and exits with a clear error if unsupported stages (like $bucket) are missing.

decision_reviews.comment: Approval of 'ready_with_gaps' is an operator choice. Events show multiple readiness approvals were logged; the build proceeded with the stated readiness level.
Choosing Python + FastAPI matches the prompt and the run environment; events show this decision was logged and the code uses FastAPI.

Choosing PyMongo and a singleton MongoClient follows driver-skill guidance; the code implements a singleton client (app/app/db.py). Events show the documentdb-driver skill was loaded when making this choice.

The decision to use DOCUMENTDB_URI from environment matches the provided run environment and is consistent with the code (app/app/db.py) and .env.example. Events show the run environment note and the log_decision recorded the choice.
Choosing separate collections customers/events and denormalized fields is consistent with the code and seed script. The code and seed both implement that design (scripts/seed.py lines 24-56).

Seeding ~1k customers was a reasonable builder choice for demo. The seed script shows NUM_CUSTOMERS configurable; the actual run used 800 customers as reported in the builder report. Events show the seed script ran and inserted sample data.
Materialising snapshots in cohort_snapshots and scheduling weekly with APScheduler is implemented (app/app/main.py scheduler lines 9-18). Decision is supported by the code and recorded in events.
Index choices were logged and implemented (scripts/seed.py lines 77-85 create indexes). Events confirm index creation via MCP queries during verification.
A later readiness approval with the same text was recorded; consistent with D001. Events show repeated readiness logs.
Re-affirmation of framework/driver choice (Python/FastAPI/PyMongo) — the code and runtime confirm this selection.
Decision to use synchronous PyMongo and singleton client is implemented in code and consistent with loaded skills.
Another readiness approval; recorded in the run and consistent with build progress.
Choosing Python + FastAPI again — consistent and supported by the code base.
Pinning to PyMongo 4.x is consistent with the compatibility docs and with the pinned requirements file present in the repo.
Decision not to provision a new cluster is consistent with the run environment and the run policy; code uses the existing cluster via DOCUMENTDB_URI.

Pinning specific dependency versions was logged with reason_source 'model_default'. The project does pin versions; this is reasonable but model_default means the choice wasn't explicitly grounded in an external compatibility doc at the time of the decision. There are public docs covering supported wire-protocols and driver compatibility (Quickstart/compatibility pages), so this is a discoverability gap more than an unsupported decision — consider citing the compatibility page when pinning.

Decision to run snapshot via python -c with sys.path.append('.') was driven by the runner refusing a PYTHONPATH= prefix; events show the 'PYTHONPATH=.' invocation was refused and that the author used an alternate approach. The 'tool_unavailable' / refusal is present in events and supports the logged reason.

doc_gaps.what_was_missing: Clear public guidance for Azure DocumentDB recommending or discouraging a DB-based lease (findOneAndUpdate) pattern for scheduled job locking.
doc_gaps.where_searched: Searches: "Azure DocumentDB findOneAndUpdate 'lease' 'distributed lock'", and installed skill docs (documentdb-*). No authoritative Azure doc prescribing this pattern was found; it remains prior-knowledge.
doc_gaps.effect_on_this_build: The sample uses APScheduler in-process and does not implement a distributed lease. For single-process demo this is fine, but a user copying the sample into multi-instance production may get overlapping jobs.
doc_gaps.proposed_content: A short 'Job scheduling and locking' page in the Agent Kit or docs that: (1) states whether Azure DocumentDB has a recommended DB-based lease pattern; (2) shows a safe example using findOneAndUpdate for a lease record (idempotent, timestamp, owner) and how to handle lease expiry; (3) shows a cloud-native alternative (use Azure Functions Timer + Durable Functions or Azure Automation + a leader-election pattern).

doc_gaps.what_was_missing: A prominent note in quickstarts/readme explaining which aggregation stages (e.g. $bucket/$bucketAuto) are supported only on certain Mongo-API server versions and how to check compatibility.
doc_gaps.where_searched: Azure feature-support pages (learn.microsoft.com) and skills (documentdb-query-optimizer). The feature-support pages mention the limitation but this guidance was not surfaced to the sample or README prominently.
doc_gaps.effect_on_this_build: The sample uses $bucket and worked against the provided cluster, but on other clusters (older server-versions) the pipeline would fail. An agent replicating the sample could build a non-working sample if it assumes $bucket is always supported.
doc_gaps.proposed_content: Add a short 'aggregation compatibility' section to sample README and to the Agent Kit: 'Before using $bucket/$bucketAuto, check your cluster server-version or run the included compatibility_check.py; if unsupported, use client-side bucketing or alternate aggregation shapes.' Include a one-liner to detect server wire-version via driver or to run a small test pipeline and explain() it.

doc_gaps.topic: JSON schema / collection validators for Mongo API
doc_gaps.what_was_missing: Authoritative guidance on whether collection-level JSON schema validators are supported and recommended for Azure DocumentDB with MongoDB compatibility (this is a prior-knowledge area with limited public docs).
doc_gaps.where_searched: Searches: 'Azure DocumentDB collection validator', '$jsonSchema operator Azure Cosmos DB', and installed skills. No clear consistent guidance found in public docs.
doc_gaps.effect_on_this_build: Sample does not create collection validators. Validators could prevent malformed documents and make aggregation assumptions safer.
doc_gaps.proposed_content: A short page in the docs/Agent Kit describing whether the MongoDB API supports collection validators for the supported server-versions, example createCollection with validator, and guidance on when to use validators vs application validation.

doc_gaps.what_was_missing: A sample or short recipe demonstrating how to call explain('executionStats') for aggregation pipelines against Azure DocumentDB and how to capture RU metrics from the explain output.
doc_gaps.where_searched: documentdb-query-optimizer skill and Azure docs; the skill mentions explain() but the sample did not include an example.
doc_gaps.effect_on_this_build: The builder did not add explain() reporting to the snapshot script; missing explain makes it harder to tune the pipeline or to show RU consumption to users.
doc_gaps.proposed_content: Add a small script (scripts/aggregation_explain.py) that runs the cohort pipeline via explain('executionStats'), prints key fields (totalDocsExamined, totalKeysExamined, executionTimeMillis, RU estimates if available) and stores the explain output to a diagnostics collection.

doc_gaps.what_was_missing: A short guide showing how to implement incremental snapshot updates using the change feed/change streams rather than full recomputes.
doc_gaps.where_searched: Azure caching docs, change feed docs and installed skills (documentdb-data-modeling, documentdb-monitoring).
doc_gaps.effect_on_this_build: The sample performs full recompute weekly; for large datasets this is RU-expensive. Lack of a small change-feed example means agents are likely to implement full recomputes by default.
doc_gaps.proposed_content: A small example showing (1) enable change feed or change streams for a collection; (2) a simple consumer that updates per-cohort aggregates on change events; (3) best-practice for checkpointing and failure handling.
